lockFileMaintenance.description: config:recommended does not enable this by default - without it, a transitive/indirect package-lock.json entry (not a direct package.json dependency) only ever gets refreshed as a side effect of some direct dependency's own bump, so a patched sub-dependency could sit unpicked-up indefinitely. This regenerates the whole lockfile within the existing semver ranges on the same weekly schedule as everything else, in its own single PR. minimumReleaseAge is explicitly unset here, overriding the 7-day global above: lock file maintenance cannot validate release age, because npm - not Renovate - decides which versions the regenerated lockfile lands on, so there is nothing for Renovate to age-check. Inheriting the global left renovate/stability-days pending forever ("Updates have not met minimum release age requirement") on a PR that was otherwise green, and the weekly regeneration restarted the clock before it could ever elapse - PR #19 sat unmergeable for three weeks that way.

customManagers.description: actionlint: ci.yml pins the download-actionlint.bash script to a commit SHA of rhysd/actionlint itself, then passes the actionlint version to download as a separate argument - keep both in lockstep. rhysd/actionlint's git tags are v-prefixed (e.g. v1.7.13) but the bare currentValue captured here (1.7.12, no v - the download script rejects a v-prefixed argument) isn't, so extractVersionTemplate strips the v from every tag Renovate compares against; without it, the digest lookup can't find an exact tag match for the bumped bare version and fails with 'Could not determine new digest'.

gitleaks CLI, downloaded and checksum-verified directly from GitHub Releases in ci.yml (not the gitleaks-action wrapper) via a GITLEAKS_VERSION env var - matching that one declaration keeps every other reference to the version in the same step (interpolated from the env var) in sync automatically.
zizmor, installed from PyPI with an exact pinned version in ci.yml.
Syft, installed and run directly (not via anchore/sbom-action) in supply-chain.yml, release.yml and container.yml via a shared SYFT_VERSION env var - keep every file in sync.
hadolint, the Containerfile linter, downloaded and checksum-verified directly from GitHub Releases in container.yml via a HADOLINT_VERSION env var.

Helm, used by ci.yml's helm job to render charts/ (and by the justfile's mirror of it) via a HELM_VERSION env var. Installed from get.helm.sh rather than GitHub Releases - the tarball and its .sha256sum both live there - but the versions are the same tags, so github-releases is still the right datasource.
kubeconform, which validates ci.yml's rendered chart manifests against the Kubernetes API schemas, via a KUBECONFORM_VERSION env var.

kube-linter, which lints the rendered Helm chart in ci.yml's helm job, via a KUBE_LINTER_VERSION env var. Unlike every other tool here it publishes no checksums file, so the install step reads the asset's sha256 from GitHub's release API instead - that tracks a bump from this manager automatically, with no hash to update by hand.

helm-unittest, the chart unit-test runner ci.yml's helm job installs into HELM_PLUGINS, via a HELM_UNITTEST_VERSION env var. It is a Helm plugin rather than a binary, but it is installed the way every other tool here is - the release tarball extracted and checked against the release's own checksum file - rather than with `helm plugin install`, which would refetch it unverified and run the release's install hook. So a bump from this manager needs no other edit. The checksum file lists its assets as ./_dist/<name>, which is why both the workflow and the justfile look the digest up by name rather than piping the file into sha256sum -c.

Trivy, the container image scanner, downloaded and checksum-verified directly from GitHub Releases in container.yml via a TRIVY_VERSION env var - not aquasecurity/trivy-action, which fetches its own binary at runtime, the same nested-fetch problem that ruled out anchore/sbom-action for Syft above.

The three bootstrap tools .devcontainer/Dockerfile has to install before `just` can take over: just itself, uv and gh. Each is pinned as an ARG and annotated with its own datasource/depName in a `# renovate:` comment, so one manager covers all three. Nothing else in that image needs a manager - every other tool there is installed by `just install-pinned`, which reads its version out of the workflow file that pins it, so the managers above already cover them.

OSV-Scanner, downloaded and checksum-verified directly from GitHub Releases via an OSV_SCANNER_VERSION env var in both container.yml (image scanning, which google/osv-scanner-action has no mode for) and osv-scan.yml (where the action was dropped because its container image pull cost 17-18s per pass against ~1s for the binary) - matched in both files so a bump keeps them in sync.

packageRules.description: Batch every uses:/container digest bump (including plain re-pins where only the SHA changed, not the version) into one weekly PR instead of one per action - this repo already reviews and merges them together.

Automerge GitHub Action digest-only re-pins once CI passes: the pinned version comment doesn't change, GitHub just moved the tag to a new commit, so there's no functional difference to review. Requires the repo's 'Allow auto-merge' setting (on) - Renovate uses GitHub's native auto-merge, which still waits for every required status check.

Automerge the workflow tool-version group (actionlint, gitleaks, zizmor, Syft, hadolint, Trivy, OSV-Scanner, Helm, kubeconform, kube-linter, helm-unittest) once CI passes - each is checksum- or SHA-verified at install time regardless of what Renovate bumps it to, and ci.yml's own actionlint/gitleaks/zizmor/helm jobs (the helm job now runs the chart unit tests as well as rendering, so a helm-unittest bump that broke an assertion would fail the PR), supply-chain.yml's sbom job and container.yml's hadolint/scan/sca jobs would fail outright if a bump broke anything. Scoped by file so the devcontainer's own three pins, which no CI job exercises, don't inherit that automerge - see the rule below.

The devcontainer's three bootstrap pins (just, uv, gh) in one weekly PR, reviewed rather than automerged: nothing in CI builds .devcontainer/Dockerfile, so unlike the workflow tools above, a bump here is only proven by someone rebuilding the container.

Batch both Containerfiles' four digest-pinned base images (Containerfile: node builder + nginx-unprivileged runtime; Containerfile.redhat: hi/nodejs builder + hi/nginx runtime) into one weekly PR. The dockerfile manager's default file patterns already match Containerfile.redhat, but matchFileNames does not - it is an exact path list here, so a new Containerfile.* must be added to it or its bases fall through both of these rules. Scoped by file because the devcontainer's base is a dockerfile-manager dep too, and gets its own rule below.

Automerge base image digest-only re-pins once CI passes: the pinned version comment doesn't change, the registry just rebuilt the same tag. container.yml genuinely exercises the new base - it builds the image, smoke-tests it running (health endpoint, real page, non-root UID, security headers) and scans it with both Trivy and OSV-Scanner - so an automerged digest bump is a tested one. That holds for Containerfile.redhat's bases too, with one caveat worth remembering: neither scanner can currently read that image (see docs/container.md), so its digest bumps are proven by the build and smoke test rather than by a scan. Version bumps (a new node or nginx release) still get a manual PR.

The devcontainer's base image gets its own PR and no automerge, unlike the Containerfile's above: nothing in CI builds .devcontainer/Dockerfile, so a digest re-pin there isn't exercised the way container.yml exercises the runtime base.

Batch every npm minor/patch bump into one weekly PR (react, vite, typescript, @codemirror/*, etc.) and automerge once CI passes (full lint/build/test/schema suite). Majors are deliberately excluded from both grouping and automerge - each gets its own PR for manual review, since a major bump is more likely to need actual code changes.
